# Phase 3, Step 2b — Phantom Continuation Rows (DIAGNOSIS ONLY)

**Nothing merged, nothing dropped, no raw CSV rewritten.** The only artefacts are this report and `data/interim/phase3_step2b_phantom.json` (gitignored). Generated by `tools/phase3_step2b_phantom.py` + `tools/phase3_step2b_report.py`; the detection net and its two structural exclusions are documented in the former's module docstring.

## 0. The defect

When a table cell wraps across a page break, camelot returns the fragment on page N+1 as its own row. Step 2's forward-fill then supplies `crop` and `active_ingredient` from the carry, and the fragment materialises as a complete-looking advisory row with empty dose columns — a **(crop, pest) pair the source never registered as a row**.

No existing check sees it: the Step 2 hard assertion counts source rows and the fragment *is* a real camelot row; the phase-2b character-conservation audit finds every character present on both sides (conservation is necessary but not sufficient for correct ROW segmentation); the bold detector sees regular-weight body text, which is what it is.

## 1. Totals

| class | count |
|---|---|
| first-row-of-page, **all four** dose cols empty | **37** |
| first-row-of-page, **some but not all** dose cols empty | **20** |
| excluded — `chemical_header`/`column_header` (dose-empty by construction) | 46 |
| excluded — non-crop-advisory sections (all semantic cols blank by construction) | 17 |

The two exclusions are structural, not judgement: a header row has every semantic column blank by construction, and a public-health/household/locust row carries `raw_row_text` only — a fragment there cannot fabricate a label claim because there is no claim to fabricate.

## 2. Which column the fragment occupies

**Fragments appear in MORE THAN ONE column.** This is the finding that changes the fix: a single pest-column merge rule is not sufficient.

| fragment column | count |
|---|---|
| `pest_or_disease` | 23 |
| *(multi-segment or no own column — see §5)* | 17 |
| `method` | 12 |
| `dilution_water` | 3 |
| `dose_formulation` | 2 |

`own_columns` is computed from the row's OWN segments (`raw_row_text`), not from its populated columns — `crop` is forward-filled on nearly every one of these rows and would otherwise dominate the signature falsely.

## 3. Scope-crop exposure

Counted across both classes, using an explicit alias map (`Red gram`/`Pigeon pea` = tur, `Bengal gram`/`Chickpea` = gram, `Grapes` = grape). `Green gram` (moong) and `Black gram`/`Urd bean` (urad) are deliberately NOT folded into scope `gram`, which is chickpea only.

| scope crop | fragments |
|---|---|
| tomato | 7 |
| cotton | 4 |
| tur | 2 |
| soybean | 2 |
| grape | 2 |
| gram | 2 |
| pomegranate | 1 |
| **total on scope crops** | **20** |

## 4. The list — all four dose columns empty

Each entry prints the previous page's last row in full, for continuation-vs-genuine judgement. `*(fwd-filled)*` marks a `crop` that came from the carry, not from this row's own text.
